newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland grain harvest 23.5-24 mln T -minister.
newsitem.headline: Poland grain harvest 23.5-24 mln T -minister.

text.p: Poland's grain harvest this year is likely to be average at around 23.5-24 million tonnes, with the grain not of very high quality, PAP news agency quoted agriculture minister Jaroslaw Kalinowski as saying on Thursday.
Some 310,000 hectares of land in southern Poland were flooded as a result of five days of heavy rain, but the agriculture ministry would not give crop loss estimates until the flood waters subsided.

"As a result of the flood there will be no shortage of grain or meat in the country. The situation will also not affect food prices. This is guaranteed by the reserves of the Agriculture Market Agency," Kalinowski was reported as saying.
Kalinowski's estimate is close to earlier forecasts by analysts, who put 1997 output at 23.4-24.5 million tonnes, against last year's 24.73 million.
Kalinowski said that because of very large grain reserves stored in the silos of grain processing firms and importers' warehouses, farmers still might have problems selling their grain at harvest.

"We are seriously worrying if there will be companies which would want to buy grain from farmers during and after harvest," Kalinowski said, adding the amount of stored grain totalled four million tonnes, twice the level of previous years.
